status_summary: Measured against the call to end engagement, federal policy has combined tariff and export-control pressure with negotiated trade: a 2025-11-01 arrangement cut a fentanyl-related tariff by 10 points, suspended an export-control affiliates rule and port-fee actions for a year in exchange for rare earth and soybean commitments, a May 2026 state visit created a U.S.-China Board of Trade and Board of Investment with purchase commitments, and the truce was extended on 2026-09-24 through 2027-01-10. On 2026-01-15 BIS moved licensing for certain advanced AI chips (such as Nvidia H200) to China from presumed denial to case-by-case review with conditions. The Supreme Court held on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, and Executive Order 14389 ended the IEEPA duties that day; Section 232 and Section 301 duties remain, including a 12.5 percent forced-labor Section 301 tariff on most Chinese goods reported in September 2026. The industrial-base goal is partly parallel through Section 232 and tariff actions, but the engagement half is materially different because trade continues under managed arrangements.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14266 raises the reciprocal tariff on Chinese goods to 125 percent.

White House fact sheet announces a China arrangement: the U.S. cuts the fentanyl-related tariff by 10 points from 2025-11-10, keeps a 10 percent reciprocal rate, suspends heightened reciprocal tariffs to 2026-11-10 and suspends the BIS affiliates rule and a Section 301 shipbuilding response for a year, while China suspends its rare earth controls and commits to soybean purchases of at least 25 million metric tons a year in 2026 to 2028.

BIS final rule revises the license review policy for certain advanced computing chips, naming the Nvidia H200: exports to China move from a presumption of denial to case-by-case review if conditions are met, including that shipments to China not exceed 50 percent of comparable shipments for U.S. end use and that an independent U.S. lab test each shipment.

Executive Order 14389 ends the IEEPA duties, including the China synthetic opioid duties and reciprocal tariffs, to stop being collected as soon as practicable; Section 232 and Section 301 duties and the suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment are unaffected.

Law-firm summary of the Supreme Court decision in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump: six Justices held that IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs; refunds were left to later proceedings.

White House fact sheet on a state visit to China: a U.S.-China Board of Trade and a Board of Investment are chartered, China approves an initial purchase of 200 Boeing aircraft and agrees to buy at least $17 billion a year of U.S. farm products in 2026 to 2028 and to address rare earth shortages.

During a state visit by Xi Jinping, the Treasury Secretary and China's Vice Premier agree to extend the trade truce through 2027-01-10; a law-firm alert reports that most Chinese goods face a 12.5 percent Section 301 forced-labor tariff after the Section 122 surcharge expired on 2026-07-24, and that the Board of Investment remains stalled.

title: End economic engagement with China and restore the manufacturing and industrial base
uncertainties: The Foreword's two halves pull in different directions in the record, so the diverged stage reflects the engagement half and the industrial-base half is only partly parallel; reshoring outcomes (manufacturing output or employment) were not measured. The Supreme Court decision was read through a law-firm summary, not the opinion, and the executive order cites only recent events; the court_status label vacated is a best fit for a holding that the tariff authority does not exist. The September 2026 truce extension, the 12.5 percent Section 301 rate and the Board of Investment status come from one law-firm alert; no White House or Treasury document was found. Section 232 actions and chip-sale licensing volumes were not tracked in detail here; see c26-04 and c21-03. Whether outbound investment and capital-market limits were tightened is covered by c22-07 and c26-06. In review, diverged was kept over a low in_progress or blocked rating: the early 2025 tariff escalation was reversed by negotiated arrangements, and the latest actions (purchase commitments, a chartered Board of Trade, a truce extended into 2027 and loosened chip licensing) maintain and manage bilateral trade rather than ending it; the industrial-base half alone would rate at most a partial parallel.
